title: Backward Hat Capital: 2 Founders of $600M Forex Fund CHARGED
summary:
Backward Hat Capital explained: on November 18, 2026, federal prosecutors in Manhattan unsealed a criminal complaint charging two of its three co-founders, Phillip Patrick Williams and Devin Allen Johnson, with securities fraud and wire-fraud and securities-fraud conspiracy. The complaint alleges the forex fund raised more than $600 million from over 2,000 investors with reported returns that typically exceeded 6% a month, paid earlier investors with new money, and sent more than $130 million to Williams. Both men are presumed innocent.
Backward Hat Capital, BH Capital, Phillip Patrick Williams, Devin Allen Johnson, alleged forex Ponzi scheme, Kokomo Indiana, AI Capital, independent audit, investment fraud charges.
All documents shown are U.S. government records; no photos of the defendants are used.
Everything in the complaint and the press release is an allegation. Williams and Johnson are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
docs_note: Documents shown are the criminal complaint in United States v. Phillip Patrick Williams and Devin Allen Johnson (S.D.N.Y., sworn Nov 17, 2026, unsealed Nov 18, 2026; page 9 cropped above the signatures) and the U.S. Attorney's Office (S.D.N.Y.) press release of November 18, 2026, re-typeset as text from justice.gov (no seals or logos). Text messages and emails are quoted only as they appear in the complaint. Claims attributed to WRTV, the Indianapolis Business Journal or Barry Minkow are their reporting or his own account, not court findings.
question: 6%+ a month on paper, month after month, with an audit calling it sound — would you have asked the hard questions? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: Prosecutors say the monthly return was set by text: "Let's do 9.91 bumped it up a bit." If your fund never had a losing month for three years, would you have pulled your money?
